I am a PhD student at Rutgers University's School of Communication and
Information, working with Kiran Garimella. My research follows misinformation
as it moves through private messaging platforms — encrypted, hard to
instrument, and increasingly the dominant medium of political talk in much
of the world — alongside parallel strands on hate-speech campaigns in
elections, peer fact-checking on WhatsApp, the accessibility of user-facing
moderation tools, and the rules people write to govern their own online
communities. Recent collaborations have taken me to the Max Planck Institute
for Demographic Research, to Cornell Tech, and to the Security, Trust &
Safety Initiative.

Before Rutgers I read computational social science at the University of
Chicago, where I worked with Molly Offer-Westort and Nick Feamster on
adaptive field-experimental tools for correcting misperceptions on Indian
WhatsApp. Earlier still I was an engineer in Bangalore — firmware at
Smarterhomes Technologies and Bosch Global Software.
